claim_boundary: Measures a capability difference between three hand-written strategies on one task. It is NOT self-improvement: no strategy was produced or improved by the system, and nothing recursive is claimed.
finding: Capability differences between strategies are measurable on this substrate for the first time. Direction: MORE elaborate is monotonically WORSE. The planning steps were written for edge-case bugs, and on a task whose difficulty is an algorithmic insight (a bitset subset sum) instructing the model to enumerate input classes appears to distract from finding it. This matches E73, where the compliance-best strategy was capability-worst.
question: On a task with capability variance, do strategies differ in SOLVING rather than in formatting?
statistical_caution: Three pairwise comparisons were made with no multiplicity correction. A Bonferroni threshold would be 0.0167, which p=0.0225 does NOT clear. The single test is therefore suggestive rather than conclusive. The monotone trend across the three strategies (60%, 30%, 20% as planning steps go 0, 3, 4) is the stronger signal, and a pre-registered trend test on fresh samples is what would settle it.
unblocks: The apparatus needed for Phase 2 now exists: a task with capability variance, a measurable improver-quality signal, and a statistical test. Having the model propose strategies and selecting on measured capability is now a runnable experiment rather than a blocked one.
validity: 20/20 for every strategy, so the differences cannot be compliance
what_it_does_not_show: No strategy was improved by anything. Three were hand-written and compared, and the best is the simplest, so no improvement has been demonstrated -- only discrimination. Phase 2 requires an improved artifact beating its ancestor on held-out tasks under matched budget; Phase 3 requires a descendant improver producing better further descendants. Neither is claimed.
